title: TAP Boot Profile
description: A TAP boot profile: a config-as-code document the bootloader (manage.py boot) applies in fixed phases to stand an instance up from a fresh, migrated database to a populated, usable instance. Profile data files live in the top-level boot/ directory (filename is the profile id). v0 carries a single population section of ordered seed-plugin / fire-collector steps; identity/auth sections and per-app schema composition are deferred (req-boot-sections). Spec: specs/spec-tap-boot-v0.md (req-boot-profile, req-boot-population).

version.description: Profile schema version. 1 for the v0 ordered-steps shape.

description.description: Human label shown by `boot --list` and in review.

profile_kind.description: Deployment-context classification of this profile, orthogonal to the plugin set. An EXPLICIT allowlist value that fail-closed guards key off (req-tap-auth-passkey-dev-bootstrap-4): a dev/local-only affordance (e.g. `manage.py enroll_admin --import-dev-passkey`, which binds an admin credential with zero proof-of-possession) is permitted ONLY under `dev_local`; `customer`/`deploy`/absent all refuse it. Omitted = unclassified = fail closed (never assume dev). This is NOT the `deploy = not settings.DEBUG` posture selector — it only TIGHTENS, never loosens. Values: `dev_local` (a developer's local multi-session / CI stack — losing this box is not a customer incident), `customer` (a customer-operated deployment), `deploy` (any non-local served deployment).

auth.description: The auth section (req-tap-auth-boot): external login providers, initial-admin emails, local-password toggle, and admin-lockout break-glass. tap_auth OWNS this section's schema (tap_auth/schemas/auth-boot-section.schema.json) and the bootloader composes it — only its object-shape is asserted here; the boot auth phase validates it strictly against the tap_auth fragment before applying. Omit for a local-password-only standup.

install.description: The install section (req-boot-install-section): the desired package-mode plugin set for this instance plus the pre-migrate snapshot switch. Consumed by the settings-free PRE-BOOT stage as plain JSON BEFORE Django starts (req-boot-preboot), separately from and earlier than `population` (which enables/seeds them) — the NetBox local_requirements.txt-vs-PLUGINS split. Build-baked plugins (hardcoded in INSTALLED_APPS during the transition to full package-mode) are NOT listed here; only plugins installed from a source. Omit for an all-build-baked instance: pre-boot install then no-ops (the snapshot still runs).

snapshot_before_migrate.description: Pre-migrate full-DB snapshot switch (req-boot-snapshot). Absent ⇒ true (safe-by-default: a prod profile that forgets the field still snapshots). This is a boot-variable: the effective value resolves flag > env (TAP_BOOT_INSTALL__SNAPSHOT_BEFORE_MIGRATE) > this profile field > default-true (req-boot-variable-resolution). Dev worktrees set the env override to false since dev DBs reset freely; a skipped snapshot logs loud (WARNING).

plugins.description: Ordered list of package-mode plugins to uv-install in pre-boot before `migrate`. Each install is idempotent: an already-satisfied plugin re-runs as a fast no-op, so a reboot does not re-pull (req-boot-preboot-3).

slug.description: The plugin slug (tap-plugin.toml `slug`), which MUST equal the plugin's `tap.plugins` entry-point key. Every enabled `seed-plugin` slug in `population` must appear here or be build-baked, else pre-boot fails the static coherence guard before `migrate` (req-boot-install-section-3).

enabled.description: false skips the install without removing it (the 'comment it out' affordance).

note.description: Free-text annotation for the human reader (e.g. why this source/rev).

source.description: Where to install the plugin from — exactly one source type. 'git' is the headline distribution path (the same mechanism as a PyPI install, source-URL only); 'editable'/'path' are for local/dev.

type.description: git: install `tap-plugin-<slug> @ git+<url>@<rev>`, pinned to an immutable revision. Requires `git` in the runtime image.

rev.description: Immutable revision (commit SHA or tag) to pin. Never a moving branch — the pin is the reproducibility + idempotency oracle (req-boot-preboot-3).

credential.description: Optional: the KEY of the source credential to authenticate this private repo (req-tap-plugin-arch-source-secret-6). Names a `<key>.secret.json` under scope `tap_plugins.source` (kind `github_pat`), resolved in pre-boot and fed to git via GIT_ASKPASS — never interpolated into `url`. Omit for a public repo, or to fall back to the fleet-wide default source credential when one is mounted. Different plugins may name different credentials to pull from different private repos/orgs in one profile.

type.description: editable: `uv pip install --editable <path>` — resolves from the source tree (dev/local).

path.description: Path to the plugin's pyproject.toml directory, relative to the repo root (e.g. 'plugins/genericom').

type.description: path: non-editable install from a local directory or a built wheel.

path.description: Path to the plugin directory or .whl, relative to the repo root.

type.description: wheelhouse: offline/airgapped install by version from a mounted directory of pre-built wheels (req-tap-plugin-arch-sources-6). `uv pip install --no-index --find-links <dir> tap-plugin-<slug>==<version>` — no network, no credential. The dir must also hold the plugins' Tier-0 PyPI dep wheels so --no-index resolves the full closure offline.

dir.description: Directory of pre-built wheels. Absolute = a mounted volume (e.g. /run/tap-wheelhouse); relative = under the repo root (dev/local).

version.description: Immutable version to install (tap-plugin-<slug>==<version>) — the reproducibility + idempotency oracle (is_satisfied = installed version matches).

required_secrets.description: Declared secret requirements for this profile's composition (req-boot-required-secrets): every secret its enabled population steps resolve at run time, so 'what must be provisioned before this profile can stand up' is answerable by reading the profile offline, from a bare clone. References only — envelope identity plus a least-privilege note; never values, never minting prose (the how-to lives with the kind's consumer-owned schema and the provisioning skill). Kept honest against the steps' secrets refs by two fail-loud coherence rules at profile load: every enabled step's ref must resolve here, and every entry must be referenced by at least one enabled step (req-boot-required-secrets-3/-4). This is one composition's config-as-code, not a TAP-kept secret inventory (doctrine: req-tap-cares-secrets-conditional-validation).

items.description: One required secret, identified exactly as its envelope under TAP_SECRETS_ROOT: <scope>/<key>.secret.json with the declared kind.

scope.description: The consuming plugin's slug — scope names the consumer, not the credential provider (req-tap-cares-secrets-consumer-scoping).

key.description: Envelope key within the scope (the file basename: <key>.secret.json).

kind.description: Expected secret kind (the envelope's 'kind' field, e.g. 'github_pat', 'aws_assumed_role'); the offline preflight fails a present-but-wrong-kind envelope loud (req-boot-required-secrets-5). Kind data schemas are consumer-owned (req-tap-cares-secrets-consumer-kinds).

note.description: One-line least-privilege statement of what the credential should be able to do (e.g. 'Fine-grained PAT, read-only, scoped to the collected repos'). Guidance for the operator/provisioning skill — never a value, never step-by-step minting prose.

population.description: The population section: ordered steps that bring plugins online and populate them. Omit for a safe, no-outbound auth-only standup (req-boot-profile-4).

on_failure.description: Behavior when a step fails. 'abort' (default): stop, skip the rest, exit non-zero. 'continue': log and proceed; exit code still signals the failure.

collector_preflight.description: Whether boot self-tests every enabled fire-collector step's collector (run_mode=self_test_only) before the first seed-plugin step mutates the grid, so dead credentials / unreachable upstreams fail in seconds with a batch verdict (req-boot-obs-preflight, spec-tap-boot-observability.md). Default true. Env override: TAP_BOOT_POPULATION__COLLECTOR_PREFLIGHT (req-boot-variable-resolution). A skip logs loud (WARNING) and is recorded with provenance in the boot record.

steps.description: Ordered list of population steps, applied strictly in array order, sequentially, with no overlap (req-boot-population-1). seed-plugin and fire-collector steps may interleave (req-boot-population-3).

type.description: seed-plugin: bring a plugin online by importing its declared GRIFT bundles via the import_plugin_grift path.

plugin.description: The plugin slug (tap-plugin.toml `slug`), e.g. 'samsite'. Resolved against loaded TAP plugins; an unknown slug aborts before any population step runs (req-boot-population-4).

bundle.description: Optional: import only this named manifest bundle instead of all of the plugin's declared bundles.

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it (the 'comment it out' affordance).

note.description: Free-text annotation for the human reader (e.g. why a step is ordered where it is).

type.description: fire-collector: fire a collector via run_collection and await its job to terminal.

key.description: The collector's qualified registry key (scope:key) exactly as stored in Collector.collector_registry, e.g. 'plugins.aws_core.collectors.boto3_collector.collector:boto3'. Resolved against the collector registry; an unknown key aborts before any population step runs (req-boot-population-4).

run_mode.description: 'full' (default) runs self-test then collect; 'self_test_only' runs only the readiness probe.

secrets.description: Secrets this step resolves at run time, as bare '<scope>:<key>' references into the top-level required_secrets manifest (req-boot-required-secrets-2). Deliberately strings, not objects — the ref is the entire step-level surface, so per-collector configuration cannot creep in here. Every ref must resolve to a required_secrets entry when the step is enabled (req-boot-required-secrets-3); fire-collector is the only step type with a runtime secret path, so only it carries this field.

items.description: One '<scope>:<key>' envelope reference — scope is the consuming plugin's slug, key the envelope basename (req-tap-cares-secrets-consumer-scoping).

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to await this collector's job to a terminal state. Omit for the bootloader default (90s); set higher for slow collectors (a full cloud pull). Per-collector default timeouts are a backlog item (req-boot-collector-timeout).

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it (the 'comment it out' affordance).

note.description: Free-text annotation for the human reader (e.g. why a step is ordered where it is).

fips_waivers.description: Operator-controlled FIPS exceptions (req-fips-crypto-bom-waivers). When the image is in FIPS mode (TAP_FIPS_MODE=1), the boot-time crypto-BOM gate refuses to serve if any crypto provider in the assembled environment (core + every installed plugin) is non-validated — a Go binary, a Rust crate on ring/aws-lc-rs, a libsodium/pynacl wheel, a JVM — because those ignore OPENSSL_CONF and silently run non-FIPS crypto. This is the deployment's escape valve: the OPERATOR (never the plugin author — a plugin cannot excuse itself from the system's FIPS posture) may accept a specific non-validated provider here, WITH a mandatory justification. Each waiver is surfaced (auditable), so every FIPS exception is explicit, not silent. Omit when there are none (the safe default: a leak fails the boot).

plugin.description: The plugin slug (or an fnmatch glob over the offending artifact's path / `dist:<name>`) whose non-validated crypto provider is being excused. A slug matches any artifact under that plugin. Provide this or `artifact`.

artifact.description: Alias for `plugin`: an explicit fnmatch glob over the finding's artifact when a slug is not the right granularity (e.g. a specific `.so` path). Provide this or `plugin`.

provider.description: The specific non-validated provider to excuse (e.g. `libsodium`, `rust-ring`, `go-crypto`, `jvm-detected`), or omit / `*` to excuse any provider on the matched artifact. Narrow it to the provider you actually reviewed.

reason.description: MANDATORY justification for accepting this non-FIPS crypto in a FIPS deployment — the whole point of the waiver. A blank reason is rejected (you cannot waive silently). State why it is acceptable (e.g. the provider is only reached for a non-security use, or the deployment's compliance authority has accepted it).
